items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: From Oliver to Jellie Roll. Now there's a guy that just goes to show you what the best New Orleans men could do with arrangements.

ctx.x: And when we play, I never like to get myself, even on the harmony parts, I like to change it around as much as possible. Even just the accents. You can still play together, but change the accents around, and it makes it sound interesting. But all those Oliver tunes had them worked out. I like working man blues. And they were like, oh, you know, you can hear. And the breaks and stuff. That was all harmony parts. And then the most classic part in that whole tune, Richard M. Jones wrote that tune. They had the…

Well, I listened to the Ori interview that Naz did. Did you ever hear that one? No. Well, Ori talks about it and he says all that was so beautifully arranged and everything except that he wasn't reading his part. No, Ori knew all that stuff. Ori knew all that stuff. Sure. But some of it was new to him, I'm sure. But he knew it almost immediately. He could just listen and grab it right away somehow. Yeah, Ori... Because he had such an ear, or had such an ear, I don't know. I haven't heard his recent records.
